pages.transcription:
Bahia, 16. I 1941

Dear Hannah and Manfred, we are now
here for three days and all what we
have seen is most wonderful; it is the most colour-
ful town I ever have met and today we assisted
the great popular festivity, the Lavagem do Bom
Fim - that means that a good part of the town,
most negro, come to wash the church in honour
of their saint and this washing which starts as
a religious ceremony and finishes in orgie of thousand
people who dance, cry, wash and become comple-
tely mad. I have never seen anything of religious
men-hysteria and all this in the brightest colours
and without any artificial tricks - there come
never strangers to see this and it would be in a
theatrical production or a film the greatest hit.
Tomorrow we are driving into the country, we
are guests of the government here and Lotte is again
photographed all day long, we send you only one
little photo of our arrival as the most are more
grotesk - myself with a little negro boy or
with the "intellectuals" of Bahia. You cannot
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier des Palace Hotel, Bahia. Die erste Zeile 'Adres: Newyork c/o Viking Press 18 East 48 Street' ist am oberen Rand notiert.

pages.transcription:
imagine what it means to see this country which is not
yet spoiled by tourists and so enormously interesting.
-today I was in the huts of the poor people who
live here practically from nothing (the bananas
and mandiocas are growing round) and the children
go like in the paradise - her whole house with
ground did cost them six dollars and so they
are proprietor for ever. It is a good lesson to see
how simply one can live and comparatively happy
-a lesson for us all, who will loose everything and
are not enough happy now by the thought how to
live then. In two days - we go tomorrow over land
to the fazendas and tobacco-factories - we will be
at Pernambuco, in five days in Belem, then after
a day in English territory (Trinidad/on the way)
to your daughter and then it will be to Lotte to
write the long letter you expect so eagerly. I
hope you feel alright and will perhaps dance
over to Bath, Lotte stands the heat and all the
excursions extremely well, only when we have
to go up in the morning at 5 or 5:30 to catch
the plane, she is hard to awaken. Fischauer is
in Rio and told me, who did not believe if he
were our communist - in any case he seems to
have saved enough money and I am like always
his admirer, how he knows to manage all with
his lying technique. Kindest regards from the
6:30 in the morning, waiting for the little time to write.
